**Finding submitted — deviation (high severity), preferred cure.**

- **Responsive clause:** Section 6.1 (p0037), read together with the Section 6.2 carve-out (p0040–p0041), HDI's own restriction in Section 6.3 (p0042), the auto-renewing term in Section 4.1 (p0024) and the survival provision (p0068, which covers only 6.3). No other restrictive covenant exists in the document.
- **Why it fails fallback:** open-ended scope ("products substantially similar", "companies similar to" named competitors) rather than a single named competing product; no internal-development or acquisitions carve-out (only closeout "Deerskin" goods); and the "during the term" hook is uncapped because the term auto-renews annually. HDI also takes an exclusive right over our own "Deerskin" brand.
- **Cure:** one surgical replace of Section 6.1 removing the Company covenant and HDI's brand exclusivity, leaving Sections 6.2 and 6.3 (the vendor-side restriction, which benefits us) and the HDI trademark licence intact; redline validated `ok:true` with the minimality gate passed. The fallback narrowing is offered in the comment.
